avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements (ferrous sulfate, ferrous gluconate)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Iron forms insoluble chelate complexes with cefdinir, reducing cefdinir absorption by up to 80% and decreasing antimicrobial efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours; take cefdinir first, then iron supplement after minimum 2-hour interval

avoid_supplements.name: Antacids containing magnesium or aluminum hydroxide
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Reduces cefdinir absorption through chelation and pH elevation in GI tract
avoid_supplements.action: Administer cefdinir at least 2 hours before or after antacid use

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics (Lactobacillus, Saccharomyces boulardii)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Antibiotics may reduce probiotic viability; probiotics may theoretically reduce antibiotic efficacy if taken simultaneously
caution_supplements.action: Consider separating by 2-3 hours; resume probiotics after antibiotic course completion

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly delay cefdinir absorption and peak serum concentrations, though clinical significance is minimal
caution_foods.action: Cefdinir can be taken with or without food; consistency in administration method is recommended

monitoring_notes: Cefdinir undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism and has few direct drug interactions. Primary concern is iron chelation reducing bioavailability; monitor for clinical treatment failure if iron supplementation cannot be separated. Screen for hypersensitivity reactions in penicillin-allergic patients (cross-reactivity ~1-3%).
